evidence_displayed: org.apache.commons.math3.stat.Frequency lines 1-560 (addValue/incrementValue; getMode body not confirmed within displayed range)
rationale: Premise 1 (test expects NaNs ignored; StatUtils.mode's javadoc promises it) is true, but it is used to attribute the fault to the method that states the convention. Premise 2 (mode -> leadingValues -> dominantEntries -> mostFrequent -> countEntries -> tabulate) matches the patch. Premise 3 correctly identifies FastMath.tabulate as adding every value, NaN included, to the Frequency, i.e. the omitted filter, and concedes Frequency honours its own contract. The chain therefore locates the divergence at the gold yet ranks the one-line delegating facade first because its documentation owns the NaN-ignore rule. mode's body computes nothing and the (sample,begin,length) overload shares the same path, so a fix there would be incomplete; only partly defensible because no intermediate helper's javadoc mentions NaN.
